scenario.question: What if the adult TTC fare rises by $0.50 next year, with Fair Pass unchanged?
missing_info: Fare elasticity measured in Toronto, by income band
How many riders sit just above the Fair Pass cutoff
Where car owners shop when they drive

sources.label: TTC merged GTFS routes and stops (district layout is simplified)
Toronto 2021 neighbourhood profiles: income and commute mode margins
UK DfT bus fare elasticities and diversion factors
Holmgren (2007), meta-analysis of public transport demand

assumptions.label: Commute fare elasticity
assumptions.note: A 10% fare rise cuts commute bus trips by about 3%. Taken from UK and international reviews, not measured in Toronto.

assumptions.label: Errand fare elasticity
assumptions.note: Shopping and other optional trips respond more strongly than commutes.

assumptions.label: Extra response for riders near the cutoff
assumptions.note: Riders with little budget room react about twice as strongly to the same fare change. Plausible from the literature, but there is no Toronto estimate.

assumptions.label: Drivers who shop at the plaza
assumptions.note: Someone who drives to run an errand often picks the big-box plaza over the corner shop.

assumptions.label: Spend per corner-shop visit
assumptions.note: Typical basket at the corner grocery or café.

assumptions.label: Sales drop before a shop cuts hours
assumptions.note: The grocery owner trims evening hours if weekly sales fall this far below week 1.

assumptions.label: Residents each agent represents
assumptions.note: Scales simulated trips and dollars up to a district of about 1,000 people.

findings.headline: Bus trips −7.3%
findings.text: In this simulated district, weekly bus trips went from 7,800 to 7,230 after the fare rose.

findings.headline: Fare revenue +$849/week
findings.text: The higher fare outweighs lost riders in this run. Across the elasticity range the change runs from +$51 to +$2,103 a week.

findings.headline: Near-cutoff riders −11.2% bus trips
findings.text: Riders just above the Fair Pass cutoff take 1.3 fewer bus trips a week and skip 0.2 more errands. Fares go from 5.6% to 5.8% of their income. Fair Pass riders stay at 3.8% and their bus use changes +0.0%.

findings.headline: Car trips +5.9%
findings.text: Car owners who leave the bus drive instead, adding about 60 car trips a week.

findings.headline: Local shop sales −3.6%
findings.text: Skipped errands and drivers choosing the plaza pull sales away from the corner grocery and café. This rests on the spending and plaza assumptions.

findings.headline: Late arrivals +0/day
findings.text: Lateness at the warehouse does not rise in this run.

findings.headline: Grocery keeps its hours
findings.text: Sales never fell past the assumed threshold, so the owner kept regular hours.

findings.headline: Could the grocery close?
findings.text: Sustained losses might threaten a small shop, but closures are not modelled here. Treat this as a question to research, not a result.
